subject: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 latency targets (Finlytics)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@finlytics.com>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap and quick clarifying questions — SLOs and latency targets

Hi Samantha / Oliver,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on your production constraints and where Redwood might help. As promised, quick recap and a few clarifying questions so our SRE/SE team can scope a focused PoC. Attaching our short SLO questionnaire (ri_slo_questionnaire.pdf).

Recap / what I heard:
- Primary goal: improve end-to-end latency for user-facing generation calls while keeping costs predictable.
- Current provider shows intermittent high tail latency around p99 during peak hours.
- You're evaluating hosted API first, with potential move to Dedicated if needed.

Clarifying questions we need answers to for sizing and PoC acceptance criteria:
1) Target E2E (client to client) latency requirements: you mentioned p95 <= 250 ms and p99 <= 700 ms as a goal — please confirm these are hard targets.
2) Current observed numbers: can you share p50/p95/p99 for your current provider, measured end-to-end (including network and any proxy)? An exported CSV or spreadsheet is perfect.
3) Throughput and concurrency: what is sustained requests per second and peak concurrent connections? Any diurnal patterns?
4) Request characteristics: typical and max input token sizes, expected response token counts, and how often you use streaming vs full-response modes.
5) Availability/SLA expectations: are you evaluating for 99.9% or higher? Any blackout windows or compliance constraints?

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm the targets above, Marissa can draft a short test plan to validate p95/p99 under realistic traffic and concurrency.
- We can provision a hosted test endpoint and run a 2-week PoC with clear acceptance criteria (p95/p99 thresholds, throughput).
- Share sample prompt set and a short list of representative routes so we can tune batching and KV cache behavior.

Attachments: ri_slo_questionnaire.pdf

I'll wait for your current metric export and confirmation on the target numbers. If you prefer a 15-min follow-up to align on exact measurement points, I can schedule.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Post-call recap and quick clarifying questions — SLOs and latency targets

Thanks Aditya — quick answers below and attached the current metrics export (finlytics_current_metrics.xlsx).

Confirmed targets:
- p95 end-to-end target: 250 ms
- p99 end-to-end target: 700 ms

Current observed (end-to-end, measured at our API gateway, 30 day window):
- p50: 210 ms
- p95: 420 ms
- p99: 1,100 ms
- Average payload: request ~420 tokens, response ~160 tokens
- Streaming: ~30% of calls use streaming (progressive token emission), 70% full-response

Throughput / concurrency:
- Sustained throughput: ~120 req/s during business hours
- Peak burst: up to 400 req/s for up to 10 minutes during report generation windows
- Typical concurrency on generator endpoints: 30-45 concurrent requests; we expect this could grow to 80 concurrent during peak events

SLA: We need 99.9% availability and tail latency guarantees for user-facing routes. If Hosted can't reach the p99 target with predictable cost, we will evaluate Dedicated.

Constraints:
- All traffic goes through our VPC egress, so network overhead is included in the numbers above.
- We can provide a sample prompt set and a short anonymized log slice.

Next: please share the SE test plan and proposed PoC acceptance criteria. We can sign an NDA if needed before sharing logs.

Thanks,
Samantha Green

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-02-11T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: initial SE notes & proposed test plan for Finlytics SLOs

Internal notes from the SE perspective after reviewing Samantha's spreadsheet and the call notes:

Key risks / observations:
- Their measured numbers include network egress and gateway latency; our hosted API in us-east will add ~20-40 ms network one-way depending on client region — we need to account for that in acceptance criteria.
- p99 of 1.1s suggests either concurrency causing queuing, cold starts, or model-side stalls. We should validate model choice and quantization profile.

Proposed PoC test plan (high level):
1) Baseline: run synthetic replay of their anonymized request traces against Redwood hosted endpoints with same payload sizes; measure p50/p95/p99 end-to-end including client-side simulated network.
2) Concurrency sweep: run tests at 30, 45, 80 concurrent connections to observe queuing and model throughput.
3) Throughput ramp: sustained 120 req/s, then 200 req/s, bursts to 400 req/s to validate autoscaling and latency impact.
4) Streaming validation: exercise streaming mode for the 30% of calls, confirm partial token emit latencies and end-to-end completion time.
5) Warm cache scenario vs cold to quantify KV/prefix cache benefits.

Acceptance criteria suggestion for Hosted PoC:
- p95 <= 250 ms for standard full-response calls at sustained 200 req/s and concurrency 45
- p99 <= 700 ms for same workload
- Streaming routes: first-byte latency p95 <= 120 ms, completion p95 <= 300 ms
- No more than 2 escalations where p99 breaches threshold during a 48 hour validated window

Data/ops needs from Finlytics:
- Sample prompt set, anonymized logs for a 1-hour high-load window
- Expected max response token lengths and percentiles

Other notes: we might need to test with both a standard open model and an optimized Redwood-verified variant. I attached a quick CSV of our internal early bench (initial_benchmark_results.csv) — these are lab numbers not adjusted for network.

If acceptable I can draft the full consolidated test plan and MAP for signature.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: initial_benchmark_results.csv
